question_text: Which of the following words is correctly spelled?

hint_ladder.title: Look for the Double Letters
hint_ladder.text: This word has a tricky spelling because it has two sets of double consonants. Think about which letters might be doubled.

hint_ladder.title: The 'cc' Rule
hint_ladder.text: The word starts with 'a', then immediately has a double 'c'. So it's 'acc...' Any option with only one 'c' is wrong.

hint_ladder.title: The 'mm' Rule
hint_ladder.text: After the 'o', there should be a double 'm'. So it's '...ommod...' Any option with only one 'm' is wrong.

hint_ladder.title: Check the Vowels Too
hint_ladder.text: The correct spelling has 'o' in the third syllable, not 'a'. So 'accommodation' is right. Look for the option that has both double 'cc', double 'mm', and the right vowels.

A.text: This one is missing an 'm'. The correct spelling has double 'mm', so 'accomodation' is a common mistake. It's easy to forget that second 'm' because the word sounds like it might only have one.

B.text: Perfect! This has both double 'cc' and double 'mm', plus the right vowels. You've got the correct spelling.

C.text: This one is missing a 'c'. The correct spelling starts with 'acc', not 'ac'. It's a sneaky error because the 'c' sound can feel like it's just one letter.

D.text: This has the right consonants but the wrong vowel. Instead of 'o' in the third syllable, it uses 'a'. So 'accomadation' is a vowel substitution error.

next_time_rule: Think of the word 'accommodation' as having a 'double bed' for both 'c' and 'm' — two 'c's and two 'm's. If you remember that, you'll never miss it.
deconstruct_text: Let's break this down together. The word 'accommodation' is one of those tricky ones that trips people up because it has two pairs of double consonants. Here's a simple way to check: start from the beginning. After the 'a', you need double 'c' — so it's 'acc'. Then, after the 'o', you need double 'm' — so it's 'ommod'. The rest is straightforward: 'ation'. So the full correct spelling is 'accommodation'. Now look at each option: Option A has 'accomodation' — that's missing one 'm'. Option C has 'acommodation' — that's missing one 'c'. Option D has 'accomadation' — that swaps the 'o' for an 'a'. Only Option B has both double letters and the right vowels. A handy trick: imagine the word as a hotel room that needs a 'double bed' for both 'c' and 'm'. Two 'c's, two 'm's — that's the key.
